symptom: Official CI verify failed when the existing Linux two-writer race test treated the partial stdout prefix RESULT: as a complete child outcome; one observed loser output lacked its trailing newline at assertion time. The new ancestor-symlink test passed, research-governance passed, and post-job cleanup succeeded. This was test orchestration, not demonstrated filesystem publication failure.
lesson: A child-process stdout data event may contain only part of a newline-delimited result. Awaiting RESULT: is not enough before exact-line comparisons; the losing process can be correctly rejected while the test spuriously fails on a missing final newline. The full job log distinguished test-harness framing from the native publication outcome and runner state.
guardrail: For synthetic concurrent subprocess tests, wait for an entire framed outcome (including its newline) before asserting exact stdout, using a non-global regex or equivalent line buffer. Preserve independent exit-code, winner/loser, stage-integrity and strict-readback assertions. Do not classify an incomplete stdout chunk as a native filesystem failure, retry an unchanged prefix-only barrier, or consume protected N2 diagnostics.
